data.text: Mutations are how clients modify data — create, update, or delete. In Hot Chocolate, mutation methods are defined on a `Mutation` class.
Create a `Mutation` class and decorate methods with `[Mutation]`. The return type becomes the GraphQL return type.

data.title: Mutation Class
data.content: Add a new book to the catalog.

data.text: Use input types to pass complex data. Hot Chocolate validates input types automatically before the resolver runs.

data.title: Input Type
data.content: Define the input for creating a book.

data.text: Update mutations typically accept an ID and an input type. Delete mutations return a boolean or the deleted object.

data.title: Update and Delete
Naming Conventions
data.text: GraphQL mutations traditionally start with a verb (addBook, not just book). Hot Chocolate preserves your method name by default.

terms.definition: A GraphQL operation that modifies data on the server.
A type used to pass structured arguments into mutations.
The data returned by a mutation, often including the modified object.

points: Use input types for complex arguments
